answer: Sybils should pay for influence itself. Each epoch a sealed-bid cipher auction sells vote weight: one encrypted bid per identity, top k=20% win, all pay the clearing price, burned. Validators verify escrowed bids, slash double-bidders, and lock escrow 3 epochs against sibling bids. Each of n sybils must outbid real demand, paying the clearing price, so total cost grows linearly in n; splitting keys cannot dodge it. Like cedar crowding one grove, each new identity thickens the market it attacks; like a lantern, the uniform price reveals what every attacker must pay.
